name: What should I do before pool demolition starts?

mainEntity.name: What prep steps should a homeowner complete before a pool removal crew arrives?
mainEntity.text: What prep steps should a homeowner complete before a pool removal crew arrives?

acceptedAnswer.text: Good preparation can prevent delays and extra charges. Before demolition starts, homeowners should remove patio furniture, toys, planters, and anything else in the work zone. Access gates, side yards, and staging areas should be cleared so equipment and debris bins can move in and out safely. The homeowner should also confirm permit status, utility marking, and whether any gas, electrical, or plumbing shutoffs are scheduled. If there are sprinkler lines, drainage features, or landscaping to preserve, those should be identified ahead of time. It is smart to ask the contractor where debris will be staged and whether nearby surfaces will be protected. A short pre-job walkthrough usually catches problems early and helps the project finish faster and cleaner.
acceptedAnswer.description: Before pool demolition, homeowners should remove furniture and loose items, confirm permit status, clear access paths, and ask the utility providers to mark or disconnect needed lines. The contractor should also verify drainage, staging space, and any landscaping to protect.
